name: Muri Ghonto
instructions: 1. Marinate the fish head with salt and turmeric, then deep-fry in mustard oil until golden; break into smaller chunks.
2. Fry potato cubes in the same oil and set aside.
3. Temper the oil with bay leaves, then sauté chopped onions, ginger-garlic paste, and tomatoes until soft.
4. Add turmeric, chili powder, cumin powder, and salt, cooking until oil separates.
5. Add the soaked Gobindobhog rice and fry for a few minutes.
6. Add the fried potatoes and fish head chunks, then pour in warm water and cover to let the rice cook until tender.
7. Finish with a generous dollop of ghee and garam masala, fluffing the rice gently before serving.
description: Muri Ghonto is a classic celebratory dish in Bengali cuisine, traditionally prepared using the head of a large fish. It highlights the Bengali culinary philosophy of 'waste not,' transforming a secondary part of the fish into a rich, flavorful centerpiece often served during weddings and special family gatherings.
